messages.author: 2c28bc819238f579
messages.subject: Error with semi-continuous space-time model
parts:
I’m trying to fit a semi-continuous spatio-temporal model to some data.  The data are weight-per-unit-effort of fish captured at survey stations, with observations either being zero (when no fish are caught) or a continuous non-zero weight.  Observations go back several years.  In modelling these data, I’ve tried to combine the methods in the semi-continuous and space-time examples in Krainski and Lingren’s very helpful R-INLA tutorial (chapters 5 and 11).  The important parts of the code are below.  While I can fit the component models successfully, the model that combines the zeros and non-zeros immediately produces an error message that means nothing to me.  Verbose=T does not produce any additional output:

##################################

Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :

  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.

  If this does help; please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

In addition: Warning message:

running command '"E:/Program Files/R/R-3.1.3/library/INLA/bin/windows/inla32.exe"  -b -s -v  -t 2  "C:/Users/ray/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpADF4zt/file80cb0dc1/Model.ini"' had status 5

##################################

 I suspect I’m messing up the index references somehow, and it doesn’t help that I don’t have a complete understanding of how the “copy” trick works here.   Any help that anyone can provide would be much appreciated. 

Thanks.

Ray


Definitions:

dat.cartesian: location of survey stations in spherical coordinates

id.station: station codes

id.year: year codes

n.yr: number of years

mesh.loc: S^2 mesh

var.dep: dependent variable (mix of zeros and continuous data)

depth.mod: station depth (covariate)


Code:

spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh.loc, alpha = 2)

#Zeros:

index.z <- inla.spde.make.index("i.z", n.spde = spde$n.spde,n.group=n.yr)

#Non-zeros:

index.nz <- inla.spde.make.index("i.nz", n.spde = spde$n.spde,n.group=n.yr)

h.spec <- list(theta=list(initial=0.2, param=c(0, 10)))

A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh.loc, loc = dat.cartesian,group=id.year)

#Zeros:

z.dep<-(var.dep>0)+0

#Non-zeros (lognormal).

nz.dep <- ifelse(var.dep>0, log(var.dep), NA)

# stack for zeros (z.dep)

z.st <- inla.stack(tag='est.z',data=list(z=z.dep,y=cbind(z.dep,NA)),A=list(A,1), effects=list(i.z=index.z,data.frame(z.b0=rep(1,length(z.dep)),depth=depth.mod)))

 

#Model  just for zeros.  No output error.

f.depth<- z ~ 0 + z.b0 + f(depth, model='rw1') + f(i.z, model=spde, group=i.z.group,control.group=list(model='ar1',hyper=h.spec))

inla.result.z<-inla(f.depth, family=c('binomial'), data=inla.stack.data(z.st),control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(z.st), compute=TRUE),control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),num.threads=2)

# stack for non-zeros (nz.dep)

nz.st <- inla.stack(tag='est.nz',data=list(nz=nz.dep,y=cbind(NA,nz.dep)),A=list(A,1), effects=list(i.nz=index.nz,data.frame(nz.b0=rep(1,length(nz.dep)),depth=depth.mod)))

# Model for non-zeros.  No output error.

f.depth<- nz ~ 0 + nz.b0 + f(depth, model='rw1') + f(i.nz, model=spde, group=i.nz.group,control.group=list(model='ar1',hyper=h.spec))

inla.result.nz<-inla(f.depth, family=c('Gaussian'), data=inla.stack.data(nz.st),control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(nz.st), compute=TRUE),control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),num.threads=2)

#Combined stack

znz.st<-inla.stack(z.st,nz.st)

#Combined model.  Outputs error copied above and nothing else.

f.depth<- y ~ 0 + z.b0 + nz.b0+ f(depth, model='rw1') + f(i.z, model=spde, group=i.z.group,control.group=list(model='ar1',hyper=h.spec)) + f(i.nz, group=i.nz.group,copy='i.z', fixed=FALSE)

inla.result.znz<-inla(f.depth, family=c('binomial','Gaussian'), data=inla.stack.data(znz.st),control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(znz.st), compute=TRUE),control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),num.threads=2,verbose=T)

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error with semi-continuous space-time model
parts:
It is hard to guess the source of such error without having a
reproducible code...

In your code you have both outcomes depending on same non-linear effect
from 'depth'. It maybe the case that it is better to have it different
for each outcome, as
... + f(z.depth, model='rw1') + f(nz.depth, model='rw1') + ...

Elias
